If you are driving on a learner permit, you need a supervising driver who meets specific rules about age and where they sit. And if you are nineteen or older, there is a waiting rule before you can apply for your license. By the end of this lesson you should know who can supervise a permit driver, including the exception for family members, and what unlocks the license application for older applicants.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Carry it every time","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Valid license or permit on your person.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-R01"]},{"text":"Every drive.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-R01"]},{"text":"Misuse: fines, jail or suspension.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every drive demands a valid license or permit on your person. Compare the permit rules on the next slide. Solo drivers just carry their papers, while permit drivers also need a supervising driver who meets the age rules. And the coach must be licensed, alert, and in the front seat. A regular license covers cars and small trucks outside the reach of the commercial license. A commercial driver's license, or CDL, covers tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tankers, larger school buses and hazmat haulers. School buses for fifteen riders sit in between, with an endorsement rather than a full CDL. Then we look at international driving permits: what they are, who issues them, what a visiting driver must carry, and why store-bought versions have no legal value. By the end of this lesson you should be able to match each vehicle to the license it needs.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Regular license and CDL","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F08","sec14-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Regular: cars and small trucks outside CDL reach.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F08","sec14-R05"]},{"text":"CDL: tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tankers.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F08","sec14-R05"]},{"text":"CDL: school buses for sixteen or more; hazmat.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F08","sec14-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"A regular license covers cars and small trucks under twenty-six thousand one pounds, outside the reach of the CDL. A CDL covers tractor-trailers, passenger buses, tankers, school buses for sixteen or more, and hazmat haulers. Put as a contrast: regular licenses cap at the weight limit outside CDL territory, while CDLs open rigs, buses, tankers, big school buses and hazmat. So if a vehicle is a tractor-trailer, a passenger bus, a tanker, a school bus for sixteen or more, or a hazmat hauler, it needs a CDL. Ordinary cars and small trucks are covered by the regular license that most drivers hold.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F08","sec14-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Fifteen versus sixteen","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fifteen-rider school bus: no CDL.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]},{"text":"Commercial and school-bus tests.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]},{"text":"Endorsement stamped with the fifteen-rider cap.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. The CDL list includes school buses for sixteen or more, which makes it easy to assume that every school bus needs a CDL. It does not. Fifteen-rider school buses skip the CDL, but they demand commercial and school-bus tests for an endorsement stamped with the fifteen-rider cap. So fifteen-rider buses need only an endorsement stamped with the cap, while buses for sixteen or more demand the full CDL. The difference is one rider. The memory line is: fifteen means endorsement, and sixteen means CDL. The endorsement still requires testing, so a fifteen-rider bus is not covered by a regular license alone.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"International permits","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"A translation for foreign travel.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-R08"]},{"text":"Licenses nothing.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-R08"]},{"text":"Issued by AAA, except to the suspended or revoked.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"International driving permits license nothing. They are translations for foreign travel. They are issued by AAA, except to drivers whose licenses are suspended or revoked. Visiting drivers in Virginia drive on their home licenses plus translations. So AAA issues permits to travelers except the suspended and revoked, and visitors must pair their home licenses with translations. The permit is not a substitute for a license, in Virginia or abroad. Its only job is to translate a license the driver already holds. And AAA does not issue them to drivers whose licenses are suspended or revoked.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Store-bought licenses","fact_ids":["sec14-F11","sec14-R07","sec14-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Store-bought international licenses: no legal value.","fact_ids":["sec14-F11","sec14-R07","sec14-F10"]},{"text":"Selling a would-be license document: Class one misdemeanor.","fact_ids":["sec14-F11","sec14-R07","sec14-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Store-bought international licenses hold no legal value, and selling any would-be license document is a Class one misdemeanor. Put as a contrast: genuine AAA permits translate for travel and license nothing, while store-bought versions license nothing legally and their sale is a Class one crime. So there are two kinds of so-called international license. The genuine one, from AAA, is a translation that licenses nothing on its own. The store-bought one has no legal value at all, and the person selling it commits a Class one misdemeanor. Neither one lets a person drive without a valid license from their home state or country.","fact_ids":["sec14-F11","sec14-R07","sec14-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the bus","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"School bus for fifteen riders.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]},{"text":"Full CDL needed?","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R06","sec14-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Dee wants to drive a school bus that carries fifteen riders. Does she need a full CDL? Work it out before reading on. The answer is no. Fifteen-rider school buses skip the CDL, but they demand commercial and school-bus tests for an endorsement stamped with the fifteen-rider cap.
